title: Et tu, Brute? How a Republic Dies

bridges.text: A father and daughter read the fall of the Roman Republic. Through shifting first-person voices - Caesar's reformer pride, Brutus's tortured idealism, Cassius's cold urgency, Antony's weaponized grief, and the hungry, steerable crowd - they trace how a republic hollows out around a beloved strongman. The Ides of March is shown as a shock silhouette, and the aftermath makes the hard point: the dagger did not bring lib Nighttime bedroom, warm lamp. Dad sits on the edge of the bed, daughter cross-legged with a thick history book open to a map of Rome. Mood shifts: curious, intimate.
Dad gestures; behind him a faded vision of the Roman Forum with togaed figures voting and arguing. Mood shifts: explanatory.
Battlefield flashback: Caesar in crimson-edged toga over armor, standing tall, laurel light around him, legions behind. Mood shifts: proud, commanding.
Wide river at dawn; Caesar on horseback at the water's edge, army waiting, Senate scroll trampled in mud. Mood shifts: defiant, fateful.
Split panel: on one side a triumph parade with banners of Caesar's face; on the other, senators in shadow watching uneasily. Mood shifts: celebratory vs uneasy.
Daughter interrupts, pointing at the book; Dad half-turned. Mood shifts: challenging, thoughtful.
Dim colonnade. Cassius, lean and sharp, grips Brutus's arm; Brutus looks tormented. Mood shifts: urgent, calculating.
Brutus alone, moonlight, holding a small bust of an ancestor; conflict on his face. Mood shifts: anguished, resolved.
Calpurnia at a window at dawn, clutching Caesar's cloak, storm outside; Caesar dressing to leave. Mood shifts: fearful, foreboding.
Interior of the Theatre of Pompey's Curia. Caesar enters among senators; conspirators drift closer, hands hidden in togas. Mood shifts: tense, closing in.
Stark shock beat: silhouette of the crowd of daggers rising against a bright window; Caesar's shadow buckling. No gore, high contrast. Mood shifts: shock, betrayal.
Brutus stands over the aftermath (off-panel body), raising a bloodless hand to a stunned, silent Senate. Doubt flickers. Mood shifts: expectant, dawning doubt.
The Forum. Antony in a vivid red cloak before a vast crowd, gesturing at Caesar's covered bier, tears becoming fire. Mood shifts: grief weaponized, rising fury.
Montage of chaos: conspirators fleeing Rome, armies massing, smoke over the city. Mood shifts: despair, ruin.
Back in the bedroom, daughter frowning at the book, Dad watching her think. Mood shifts: reflective, sobered.
Dad closes the book gently; daughter looks resolved. Faint modern city skyline reflected in the window behind them. Mood shifts: warm, resolved, hopeful.
